title: A Strange Offer
description:
Near Exit 11 at Gangnam Station. Late afternoon.

About to walk past when a man spoke up.

Worn jacket, clean envelope. Eyes unusually sharp.

"Want to make money? More precisely — do you need information?"

Crowded street. Easy to walk away.

choices.result_text: The man pulled the envelope closer.

Walked past. The man said nothing from behind.

Three blocks later, glanced back.
Already gone.

What that was — will never be known.

title: The Price of Information
description:
The man spoke.

"One of the Mapo redevelopment zones gets project approval this month. Not announced yet. I have a source."

"₩500,000. Cash. Now."

No way to know if it's real or a scam.
How much ₩500,000 weighs depends on what's in the account right now.

choices.result_text:
Took the envelope. Dense with district names and lot numbers.

The man handed it over and walked away without looking back.

{name} put the envelope in the bag. The answer comes in three months.

choices.text: Still feels like a scam. Don't buy it
choices.result_text:
"I'll think about it." Turned and left.

The man didn't try to stop him.

At home, searched Mapo redevelopment news.
Nothing yet.

title: 3 Months Later — The Article
description:
A portal news notification.

'Mapo District ○○ Zone Redevelopment Final Approval — Property Surge Expected'

{name} took out the envelope. The lot numbers matched.

Three months ago. The man near Gangnam Station.

choices.text: Invest immediately in a small stake in the area
choices.result_text:
The area's asking price rose 30% by announcement day.

{name} walked away with ₩8,000,000. 16x the investment.

Still don't know who that man was.
Might never meet him again.
Seoul has people like that.

choices.text: Already gone up. Don't chase the price
choices.result_text:
The information was correct. But couldn't execute the investment.

The second trap of investing — having the right information and still missing the return.
The first trap is believing the wrong information.
The second is missing the timing on the right one.

₩500,000 tuition.

title: 3 Months Later — Nothing Happened
description:
Searched Mapo redevelopment.

Nothing. The lots were still in a greenbelt zone.

The man was just a scammer.

₩500,000.

choices.result_text:
₩500,000.

Expensive lesson. Still a lesson.

Buying possibly illegal insider information was also wrong. He knew that and came anyway.
It wasn't being victimized. It was participating.

That thought was the bitterest part.

Went to the station. Filed a statement.

But without better identifying information, tracking him would be difficult.
Similar cases on record, they said.

Getting the ₩500,000 back was unlikely.
But said something. That's all that could be done.

title: Seat Next to a Stranger
description:
Late night pojangmacha. Drinking alone.

A drunk man in his 50s sat down next to {name}.

"My company's gone. Ten years of building it. Final decision came today."

The man pulled out a business card. Name of a company that no longer existed.
Handed the card to {name}. "Call me. I might be able to help."

choices.result_text:
The man drank two more rounds then got up first.

"I can pour out everything I learned in ten years. No money, but."

Put the card in the wallet. Might call. Might not.

The man kept drinking. {name} too.

At the end the man left first. The card stayed on the table.

{name} left it there.

title: 5 Months Later — That Number
description:
A crumpled business card came out of the wallet.

The pojangmacha. The CEO whose company failed.

Took it without much expectation.

Sent a text. "This is the person who took your card that night."

Thirty minutes later, the phone rang.

choices.result_text:
Three hours at a café.

He poured out everything from ten years — supplier negotiations, managing employees, investor meetings, and why it all fell apart.

"Learning from someone who failed is the cheapest education. Successful people don't tell you the real things."

This was worth more than that ₩500,000.

choices.text: He was just drunk. Don't reach out.
choices.result_text:
Threw the card out.

Just one of those nights.

title: The Empty Line on the Resume
description:
Filling out a job application — stopped.

English proficiency. Typed TOEIC 900.

Actual score: 745.

Application deadline in two hours. No time for a retest.

choices.result_text:
Submitted 745.

Made it to the interview. The interviewer looked at the score and said "a bit low."
{name} answered "I'm working on it."

Whether it led to an offer or not — unknown. But didn't lie.

choices.text: Write 900. Deal with it if caught.
choices.result_text:
Submitted.

Passed the document screen. Interview scheduled.

Night before the interview — what if they ask for proof?
That thought didn't leave all night.

title: 4 Months Later — HR Summons
description:
An email from HR.

"As part of the onboarding document verification process, we need to confirm the original language test score."

{name} read the email three times.

The office was quiet. Seoul was outside the window.

choices.result_text:
Bowed in front of the HR manager.
"My score at the time of application was lower and I recorded it incorrectly."

That was the truth.

Processed as a recommended resignation.

Hard to make eye contact with coworkers while packing up.
Didn't expect to be starting over in Seoul this fast.

choices.text: Forge the transcript and submit it
choices.result_text:
Found a method online. Modified the file.

Submitted. Passed.

Drank that evening. Couldn't get drunk.
Now one more person knows about this.
That person is {name}.

title: USB
description:
A USB drive sitting on the break room table.

No label. Been there for a week.

No lost-and-found notice posted. Might be abandoned.

choices.result_text:
A folder with no company logo.

Files opened. Spreadsheets. Numbers.

Shouldn't be looking at this. Already looking.
Supplier list, unit prices, contract terms.
Information a competitor would want.

{name} pulled out the USB.

choices.text: Take it to the general affairs team
choices.result_text:
They were grateful.
"Oh, this went missing last month. Thank you."

Small thing. But that person included {name} at the team dinner next month.
In Seoul, reputation gets built in places like this.

title: What's on the USB
description:
A week passed.

Those files won't leave {name}'s head.

A competitor supplying the same products at 30% below this company's costs.

The question is what to do with this information.

choices.text: Report to the team lead — this benefits the company
choices.result_text:
The team lead listened quietly.
"How did you find out?"
"Found it in the break room. File was already open."

True.

The lead escalated to legal. Didn't share the outcome with {name}.
But at month's end, said: "Good work. Genuinely."

Put the USB in a drawer and forgot about it.

Two months later, that competitor was in the news.
Alleged trade secret leak.

{name} opened the drawer. The USB was there.
Threw it out.

title: KakaoTalk After 5 Years
description:
A KakaoTalk notification.

'Hey, doing well? Remember me?'

No profile photo. Name not saved.
Looking at the number — seemed like someone from a university group project.

No contact for five years, and suddenly.

choices.result_text:
"Yeah, I remember. You been okay?"

Started texting once or twice a month.
Turns out they were starting an interior design company.

Just ordinary day-to-day talk. But weirdly looked forward to it sometimes.
One more old contact brought back to life in Seoul.

choices.text: Leave it on read. Why now.
choices.result_text:
Read it. Didn't reply.

They didn't reach out again.

A week later, saw on SNS they'd co-founded some company.
{name} closed the post without hitting like.
